concept.name: Ease of movement
concept.definition: Richard Arms' oscillator relating midpoint change to volume and range: it measures how much price moved per unit of volume, rising when prices advance with ease (large range, light volume) and falling when they decline with ease.
concept.intuition: If a big price move needs little volume, movement is 'easy'; if heavy volume produces a tiny range, movement is labored - EMV quantifies the effort-versus-result idea behind Arms' Equivolume charts.
concept.mechanics: Distance moved = midpoint_t - midpoint_{t-1} with midpoint = (H+L)/2; Box ratio = (V / 100,000,000) / (H - L); 1-period EMV = distance / box ratio; the traded indicator is a 14-period SMA of 1-period EMV. Positive readings mean rising with ease, negative falling with ease.
concept.formula: EMV = ((H+L)/2 - (H_prev+L_prev)/2) / ((V/100,000,000)/(H-L)); EMV(14) = SMA(1-period EMV, 14); the volume scale divisor is platform-dependent.
concept.failure_modes: The volume scale divisor is arbitrary and platform-dependent, so absolute values are not comparable across platforms; tiny-range or low-volume bars make the ratio explode into spikes.
concept.misconceptions: A high positive EMV is not automatically bullish strength - it can simply mean price drifted up on falling volume, which many traders read as weakness.
concept.example: If the midpoint rises 1.00 on volume of 20M and a range of 2.00, the box ratio is 0.2/2 = 0.1 and 1-period EMV = 10.0 - an 'easy' advance.
